title: Bare-name phase 1: refuse a second package holding a non-object name whose consumers resolve without package context (ruling C on #30798)
body:
epic:#3600#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjPXwX1YfHyKJUh4agu

Filing-gate category: ② execution of a maintainer ruling. Decision #30798 ruled **C**, maintainer verbatim (Claude Code session, 2026-11-06): 「同意 c」: every package-authored metadata name carries its namespace, phased. Routing, verbatim: 「能交给车队开发的你不要自己开发」.

Phase 1 of 3. Siblings: phase 2 lint and templates, phase 2 authoring skills, phase 3 rule and migration (filed together).

## Problem (customer-visible)

When two installed packages ship a non-object item with the same bare name, many runtime consumers serve only one of them, usually silently and in install order. Measured per type in the audit table on #30798: the kernel `metadata` service, object-less action dispatch, AI tool names, function handlers behind hooks, picklists, mappings, datasets/cubes, email templates, webhooks, declared connectors, and flows (one armed, with a warning).

## Ask

1. **Measure first.** Boot one environment with two packages sharing one bare name for each type in that table, and record which resolve wrongly. The table is a code reading, not a booted measurement.
2. Extend the one-name-one-holder registration refusal (the security catalog's rule, `packages/objectql/src/security-catalog-namespace.ts`; precedent #22197 +1080/−103 and #22365 +705/−43) to every type the measurement shows resolving without package context. The refusal applies at managed install, at package registration and at cold boot (as #22307 did), names both holders, and carries the rename in the message.
3. Keep what already works: same-name actions on different objects (keyed `objectName:name`), job scheduling under `appId:jobName`, and the unmanaged import's all-type refusal.
4. Record the narrowing on ADR-0048 §3.4. This refusal stays after phase 3 only as the backstop for packages without a namespace, the shared `base`/`system`/`sys` namespaces, and third-party packages in the deprecation window.

Out of scope: the types a separate security item covers. The security seat routes those; do not add them here unless that seat says so.

Reader: the `domain:engine` lane seat, from `pm:queue`.
